chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Abu al-Jawza', from al-Husayn ibn 'Alwan, 'Amr ibn Khalid, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The vow is of two types: that which is for Allah and that which is for other than Allah; its expiation is the expiation of an oath.
ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for breaking a vow in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Isfabar, Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between vows dedicated to Allah and those dedicated to other entities, ruling that the expiation for breaking either is equivalent to that of an oath (kaffarat yamin). This ruling aligns with the Shia view that the specific object of the vow does not alter the penalty for its violation, emphasizing the binding nature of the vow as a solemn commitment. The classification underscores the practical application of kaffarat in daily religious observance, ensuring consistency in legal rulings regardless of the vow's recipient.
